paper_title: Axion Dark Matter from Cosmic String Network
notes: This paper is a lattice simulation study of axion dark matter production from cosmic string networks in the post-inflationary scenario. While the abstract and title mention 'derive a lower bound on the axion mass' (Section 8.1), the actual numerical bound is NOT clearly stated in the provided excerpt. The paper discusses: (1) logarithmic growth of string number density ξ ∝ log(m_r/H); (2) power-law spectral index q of axion emission with q ∼ 0.5-1.0 in the simulation range, extrapolating to q ∼ 1 at log(m_r/H) ≈ 70 (QCD crossover); (3) axion abundance calculations comparing string-radiated axions to misalignment mechanism. Section 8.1 states 'The lower bound on the axion mass can be derived by requiring that the axion dark matter abundance does not exceed the currently observed value' and references Ω_a h² ≈ 0.12 (28 µeV/m_a)^(7/6), but the actual numerical lower bound value is cut off in the provided text (marked as '===RESULTS_EXCERPT (limit statements beyond the first 60000 chars)==='), making extraction impossible. The paper does NOT present an exclusion plot with (m_a, f_a) or (m_a, coupling) pairs that would constitute a standard AxionMass limit. Instead, it provides simulation predictions of the axion spectrum and abundance as functions of cosmological parameters. Without the explicit numerical bound statement, this cannot be classified as a measured exclusion limit. The coupling_type AxionMass is appropriate IF the bound were stated, but data_points cannot be populated without the actual numerical result.
